tasks.short: Check collection notices and identification, then release held letters or packages and record collection.

steps.what: Receive the collection notice or collection reference.
Find the held-item record and authorised recipient in the collection log.
Check identification and any authority to collect for another person.
Retrieve the held item and match its label to the collection record.
Approve release, hand over the item, and obtain acknowledgement.
Mark the item collected and file the receipt.

tasks.design: Configure a collection register in the {WORKFLOW} with item references, storage locations and authorised recipients. Scanning a reference retrieves the record; the clerk checks identity and approves physical release, after which the register stores the receipt and closes the item.
tasks.previous_blocker: Paper notices and storage records were separate. A digital register still could not verify the person standing at the counter.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing forms, barcode fields and receipt workflows can handle the records. AI-assisted coding makes small gaps cheaper to fill; no model is needed.
tasks.still_hard: Delegated collection, missing notices and disputed identity need judgement. GDPR requires limited access and proportionate retention of identity-related records.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise suspicious or unclear collection attempts and explain a refusal without exposing another person's correspondence.

ambition.what: Pre-arranged delegated collection for employees unable to attend

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time searching logs and more time resolving collection problems. With delegated authority, they can approve routine collection arrangements within a defined policy.

reach.learn: Authorisation requirements, service accessibility and escalation limits

evidence.claim: A reference-based register can automate lookup and collection records while physical identity checks remain human.

assumptions: Held items have unique references and identifiable storage locations.
A configurable {WORKFLOW} is available.
Remaining-time estimates are design priors, not measured savings.
Access planning includes GDPR review and employee consultation where national rules require it.
unknowns: Current collection log format and item volumes
Accepted identification and delegated collection rules
Existing platform access and receipt retention requirements
Whether the clerk can approve routine collection arrangements
research_questions: Can the available {WORKFLOW} capture receipts without retaining identification copies?
Which national rules affect employee consultation for the collection register?
new_work: Resolve unmatched references and disputed authorisations.
Maintain storage locations and recipient permissions.
Check failed receipt updates and apply retention rules.

tasks.short: Move sorted mail containers and parcels to their designated holding or dispatch areas.

steps.what: Check container labels against designated holding or dispatch areas.
Remove, move and place containers safely in their designated areas.

tasks.design: Use standard destination labels and matching signs before adding software. Where destinations change frequently, configure a barcode lookup in the {WORKFLOW} to show the current area; the clerk still moves and places the containers.
tasks.previous_blocker: Most time is physical handling. Automating destination lookup alone offered limited savings.
tasks.enabler_now: Simple label standards and configurable lookup screens are inexpensive. No advance in model capability is required.
tasks.still_hard: Weight, stairs, congestion and awkward containers remain physical constraints. Software cannot replace safe lifting or suitable equipment.
tasks.human_edge: Spot unstable loads, blocked routes and damaged containers before moving them.
tasks.altitude: The week remains dominated by physical handling, with fewer destination checks. Decision rights do not change.

reach.task: Arrange staging areas around collection times
reach.learn: Load limits, handling equipment and staging discipline

evidence.claim: Destination labels and barcode lookups can simplify checks but do not automate container movement.

assumptions: Containers are moved with existing carts or handling equipment.
Labels can use destination codes without exposing correspondence contents.
The optional lookup uses an existing {WORKFLOW}.
The label-check time estimate needs local validation.
Access planning includes employee consultation where national rules apply.
unknowns: Container weights, travel distances and handling equipment
Whether unclear labels cause meaningful delays
research_questions: Would fixed destination signs remove enough checking to avoid a software build?
Can staging areas be arranged to reduce repeated handling?
new_work: Replace unreadable labels and maintain destination signs.
Update the optional lookup when staging areas change.

tasks.short: Choose a mailing service, prepare dispatch documents, and hand outgoing mail or parcels to the carrier.

steps.what: Read the sender's destination, deadline and handling instructions.
Weigh and measure the item and check its physical handling needs.
Select service in the {OTHER} carrier booking system using requirements, measurements and tariffs.
Book postage and generate labels and the dispatch manifest.
Attach labels and group items by carrier and collection time.
Check the dispatch batch and release it to the carrier.

tasks.design: Replace free-text dispatch requests with required fields in the {WORKFLOW}, and configure service rules in the {OTHER} carrier booking system. Connect measurements and the {PARTNER_PORTAL} to generate bookings, labels and manifests within approved spending limits; exceptions pause for review, and the clerk approves physical handover.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sender instructions, measurements and carrier tariffs arrived separately. Small integration projects cost more than the repeated manual choices appeared to justify.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured forms and existing service rules remove interpretation. AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of connecting measurement devices and booking interfaces.
tasks.still_hard: Restricted contents, international documentation and unusual delivery guarantees need specialist checks. Carrier interfaces and tariff changes create ongoing maintenance.
tasks.human_edge: Notice packaging or contents that make an otherwise valid service choice unsuitable.

ambition.what: Review recurring urgent-mail causes each week

tasks.altitude: Routine service selection and paperwork shrink, leaving time to identify avoidable urgent dispatches. With management delegation, the clerk can recommend revised collection cutoffs and approve routine service substitutions within budget.

reach.task: Compare mailing service cost and delivery performance
reach.learn: Contract tariffs, delivery commitments and fair comparisons across shipment types

evidence.claim: Structured shipment fields and tariff rules can automate routine service selection and dispatch document generation.

assumptions: Routine bookings have approved tariffs and spending limits.
Senders enter dispatch requirements through the replacement form.
The {OTHER} carrier booking system supports service rules.
Measurement devices and carrier interfaces support integration.
Remaining-time estimates exclude exceptional shipments.
Access planning includes GDPR controls and consultation where national rules require it.
unknowns: Current request channels and carrier booking tools
Contract tariffs, spending limits and permitted services
Device connectivity and booking interface access
Volume of international or restricted-content shipments
Authority to change cutoffs or substitute services
research_questions: Which service rules can be configured directly in the existing booking system?
How are duplicate bookings prevented and failed bookings reconciled?
Which shipment types require an explicit approval before booking?
new_work: Maintain tariffs, service rules and collection cutoffs.
Review requests that fail address, spending or handling checks.
Reconcile booking failures and duplicate labels.
Review recurring urgent dispatches with sending teams.

tasks.short: Identify incoming mail recipients, sort delivery batches, distribute mail, and collect outgoing items.

steps.what: Read recipient names, departments and handling markings on incoming mail.

loop.input: Envelope address images and handling markings; existing structured labels bypass the loop.
loop.output: Recipient name, department and handling flags with image references.
loop.check: Validate fields against the recipient directory; unreadable, conflicting or private markings enter review.
loop.stop: One extraction attempt per envelope; unresolved fields go to the clerk without automatic routing.
loop.why_not_simpler: Sender labels vary and may contain free text. Exact matching handles structured labels first.

steps.what: Check the recipient directory and resolve unclear or outdated destinations.
Sort incoming items into recipient or department delivery batches.
Deliver incoming mail to designated desks, mail points or collection areas.
Collect outgoing mail from mail points and return it to the mailroom.

tasks.design: Connect a permitted recipient directory from the {HCM} and location records in the {DOCS} to the {WORKFLOW}. Read structured envelope labels directly and use one bounded extraction loop for irregular addresses, then apply exact routing rules and send ambiguous items to the clerk. The {WORKFLOW} provides ordered delivery lists and collection alerts through the {EMAIL}; physical sorting and movement remain with the clerk.
tasks.previous_blocker: Envelope formats varied and recipient locations went stale. Physical sorting and delivery still accounted for much of the work.
tasks.enabler_now: Document extraction can handle irregular address text, while deterministic directory matching controls routing. Small integrations are cheaper to build and maintain.
tasks.still_hard: Similar names, former employees and confidential markings create exceptions. GDPR applies to envelope images and recipient records; assess the intended use under the EU AI Act and consultation under national rules.
tasks.human_edge: Resolve ambiguous recipients discreetly and recognise items needing special handling without opening private correspondence.

ambition.what: Collection alerts for employees who work away from the office

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time deciphering addresses and searching directories, but still sorts and transports mail. With delegation, they can arrange collection options for remote employees and choose routine delivery routes.

reach.task: Plan mail points for hybrid working patterns
reach.learn: Building access, secure storage and accessible collection arrangements

evidence.claim: Business post can be scanned and forms converted into data.
A documented insurance mailroom case shows that correspondence administration can be partly automated.
Envelope extraction followed by directory rules is a proposed application; the cited cases do not establish savings for physical sorting or delivery.

assumptions: The directory exposes only fields needed for mail routing.
Envelope capture does not require opening correspondence.
Clear directory matches may route automatically; ambiguous matches are held.
Delivery time may fall modestly through route ordering; this needs measurement.
Consultation estimates include employee representatives where national rules apply.
The design does not introduce individual worker-speed monitoring.
unknowns: Daily mail volume and proportion of irregular addresses
Current directory accuracy and access permissions
Existing scanning equipment and lawful image retention periods
Rules for confidential, former-employee and undeliverable mail
research_questions: How accurately can envelope fields be extracted on a representative local sample?
Can directory matching distinguish similar names without additional personal data?
Does route ordering reduce walking enough to justify its upkeep?
Which employee groups need private collection alerts?
new_work: Capture envelope images and review extraction exceptions.
Correct stale directory entries through the authorised record owner.
Maintain routing rules and special-handling flags.
Manage image retention, access and failed collection alerts.
Check routing errors across label formats without ranking individual clerks.

role.altitude: Physical handling remains the largest part of the job. Less lookup and dispatch paperwork creates room for secure collection services, delivery planning and resolving unusual mail; wider decision rights require explicit delegation.
reach: Administrative services manager: delegated collection and accessible mail services
Facilities manager: secure mail points and collection arrangements
Logistics analyst: dispatch cost and delivery performance
Shipping, receiving, and inventory clerk: safe staging and handling
skills_to_grow: Measure service delays and routing errors
role.ambitious_version: Run a small workplace correspondence service with secure collection options for remote employees, reliable routing and weekly reviews of avoidable urgent dispatches.

job.title: Mail Clerks and Mail Machine Operators, Except Postal Service
